 Irish Give No 1 Florida A Battle But Fall 86 78 
 Jeffrey Myers Featured in this article Brady Koehler Logan Imes Braeden Shrewsberry Jonathan Sanderson Logan Duncomb Ethan Roberts Braeden Smith Irish Give No. 1 Florida A Battle, But Fall 86-78
 Shrewsberry and Koehler combined for 30 points in the second half November 17, 2026 Twitter Facebook Email Featured in this article Brady Koehler Logan Imes Braeden Shrewsberry Jonathan Sanderson Logan Duncomb Ethan Roberts Braeden Smith PDF Box 
 LAS VEGAS - The Notre Dame men's basketball team gave the No. 1 team in the country everything they had in the second half, cutting a 16-point deficit to Florida to three. The Gators (5-0) built the lead back to 14, but the Fighting Irish (4-1) answered again, cutting it back to six. The Irish knocked on the door several times but ultimately fell 86-78 in the opening round of the Players Era 8 tournament. 
 As a result, the Irish will now play Rutgers at 2 p.m. ET on Wednesday, airing live on ESPN. 
 Braeden Shrewsberry and Brady Koehler combined for 30 points in the second half. Shrewsberry drained 5-for-6 from deep in the half, ultimately finishing with a season-best 20 points. It marked his 12th 20-plus point performance of his career. 
 Koehler was 5-for-11 in the second half for 14 points, finishing with 17 for the game. Koehler has now tallied at least 14 points in all five games to start the year. Both Koehler and Shrewsberry tied for a team best five boards today. 
 Another bright spot today was Jonathan Sanderson , who posted his second straight game in double figures. The freshman had 10 points by half, and then finished with a season-best 14 for the game. 
 Rounding out the Irish double-digit scorers was Ethan Roberts , who finished with 10 behind a 6-for-6 effort from the free-throw line. Braeden Smith once again led the squad in assists with five on Tuesday.   
 Notre Dame shot 49.1 percent from the field compared to Florida’s 52.7 percent. The difference maker was on the glass and in second-chance points. The Gators outrebounded the Irish 38-22 (offensive rebounds were 15-4), earning a 26-6 advantage in second-chance points. Florida also posted 42 points in the paint. 
 HOW IT HAPPENED  
 Florida worked it down low to start the game on an 8-0 run, all points in the paint. The Irish missed their first four shots before Braeden Smith landed the first bucket at the 15:29 mark. 
 Notre Dame forced four turnovers early to keep it close, as a Brady Koehler three at 13:30 made it a five-point game at 10-5. 
 It was ultimately a 1-for-6 start from beyond the arc for Notre Dame, falling behind 15-5, until Logan Imes and Jonathan Sanderson gave the offense a spark off the bench with back-to-back triples. Logan Duncomb then made it an 8-0 run over 1:41, prompting a Florida timeout, now down just 15-13. 
 Out of the timeout, the Gators responded with buckets on back-to-back possessions, driving their lead back up to six. 
 The Irish countered with a 5-0 run on a floater from Imes and an old-fashioned three-point play from Sanderson to bring the Irish within one. 
 A pair of free throws from Roberts and a pullup jumper from Smith kept the Irish within three at 25-25, but back-to-back three-pointers from the Gators extended the Florida lead to nine with just under five minutes left in the half. 
 This sparked what would turn into a 13-2 run to make it 38-22 with 2:55 remaining. The Gators ultimately outscored the Irish 22-10 to end the half, securing a 47-32 halftime lead. 
 From the time it was 25-22 Florida with 5:11 remaining, the Gators ended the half shooting 6-of-8 from the field, which included four made triples, plus six from the free-throw line. 
 Notre Dame shot 12-of-26 (.462) in the half, 3-of-12 (.250) from deep and 5-for-5 from the line, compared to Florida’s split of 16-of-26 (.615), 5-of-7 (.714) and 10-for-14. The Gators owned the glass 20-7, recording 14 second-chance points. The Irish forced nine Gator turnovers, which they converted into nine points. 
 Brady Koehler scored nine points in the first 3.5 minutes to get the Irish off to a 12-5 second-half start. Florida countered with a quick 5-0 run to head into the first media timeout, up 57-44. 
 Shrewsberry then ignited a 10-2 run with a pair of triples to cut the deficit to five at 59-54. A pair of Imes free throws then made it a one-possession game with 11:26 left. 
 Next, the Gators punched back, using their size to get boards and to the line, recording a 9-0 run in under two minutes and ultimately building a 14-point lead. 
 However, the Irish kept fighting, this time behind a Shrewsberry heater. The senior knocked down two more triples to power an 8-0 run. Once again, Notre Dame was knocking on the door down six, 76-70, with just 4:26 left. 
 Florida’s Condon and Klavzar powered the Gator lead back to 10 with one minute remaining, and a Sanderson layup cut it to eight as the Irish applied a full-court press in hopes of forcing a turnover and regaining possession. 
 The two squads would exchange free throws to close it out as the Irish fell to No. 1 Florida, 78-86.
 UP NEXT 
 Notre Dame will now play in Wednesday’s consolation game No. 1, which pits the Blue & Gold against Rutgers. That game is slated to tip off at 2 p.m. ET on ESPN. It’ll mark the third consecutive year in which Notre Dame and Rutgers will clash at Players Era, with the recent series split 1-1 in Vegas.
